knowledge:
- key_parameters: pedigree=A data.frame or file path containing pedigree data (family, id, father, mother, sex) ;; age=Optional vector of ages or endages for individuals ;; trait=A vector representing trait status (0/FALSE for unaffected, 1/TRUE for affected) ;; nsim=Number of Monte Carlo simulations to perform ;; strata=Vector for stratified sampling (e.g., sex matching) ;; controlSetMethod=Method to define control sets (e.g., "getSexMatched", "getExternalMatched") ;; timeAtRisk=Vector representing time at risk (e.g., age of onset or death) for FIR ;; prob=Population-based probability of being affected for the binomial test ;; prune=Logical, if TRUE, extracts/plots the smallest possible pedigree for a list of individuals
- alternatives: kinship2=Used internally for kinship coefficient calculations and pedigree plotting, but switch to Pedixplorer is recommended for R <= 4.5 ;; HaploPainter=Perl script that can be used as an alternative plotting backend via switchPlotfun("haplopaint") ;; gap=Contains the gif function, which calculates the genealogical index of familiality but does not estimate significance ;; igraph=Used internally or via ped2graph to represent pedigrees as graphs
- when_to_use: Use when you have large pedigree data and trait information (e.g., disease status) and want to identify families or individuals with significant familial clustering/aggregation of the trait, or to select promising individuals for sequencing projects.
- pitfalls: Singletons (unconnected individuals) are excluded by default in several tests (e.g., GIF, FIR) or return NA because kinship-based statistics cannot be estimated for them ;; Stratified sampling or matching can lead to the exclusion of individuals with missing values in the matching criteria or strata ;; Systematic bias in datasets (e.g., ascertainment bias where families are only included if a founder is affected) can distort results ;; HaploPainter only allows exporting plots to a file, whereas kinship2 allows standard R plotting.

workflows.name: pedigree_management_and_visualization
workflows.intent: Import pedigree data, manipulate relationships, prune pedigrees, and visualize them as standard pedigree plots or graphs.
input: pedigree_data.txt (a tab-delimited text file containing pedigree columns: family, id, father, mother, sex)
workflows.stages: 1. Create FAData object from file or data.frame ;; 2. Extract family or individual pedigree information ;; 3. Find founders or common ancestors ;; 4. Plot pedigrees ;; 5. Convert pedigree to graph and find subgraphs
workflows.code:
fad <- FAData(pedigree = mbped, age = endage)
head(pedigree(fad))
head(fad$father)
head(family(fad, family = 4))
switchPlotfun("ks2paint")
plotPed(fad, id = 3, device = "plot")
fullPed <- buildPed(fad, id = "3")
buildPed(fad, id = c(21, 22, 17), prune = TRUE)
plotPed(fad, id = c(21, 22, 17), prune = TRUE)
findFounders(fad, "4")
getCommonAncestor(fad, id = c(21, 22, 17))
getChildren(fad, id = "4", max.generations = 1)
getAncestors(fad, id = "4")
getSiblings(fad, id = c("4"))
fullGraph <- ped2graph(pedigree(fad))
singleFam <- ped2graph(family(fad, family=4))
subgr <- connectedSubgraph(singleFam, nodes = c("7", "8", "27", "17"))
pedFile <- system.file("txt/minnbreastsub.ped.gz", package = "FamAgg")
fad <- FAData(pedFile)
export(fam4, tmpF, format = "ped")

workflows.name: familial_aggregation_testing
workflows.intent: Evaluate familial clustering of traits using various statistical tests (GIF, FIR, Kinship Sum, Kinship Group, Binomial).
workflows.stages: 1. Set trait information on FAData ;; 2. Run Genealogical Index of Familiality test ;; 3. Calculate Familial Incidence Rate (FIR) ;; 4. Run Kinship Sum test ;; 5. Run Kinship Group test ;; 6. Run Binomial test ;; 7. Plot test results
workflows.code:
trait(fad) <- cancer
gi <- genealogicalIndexTest(fad, trait = tcancer, traitName = "cancer", nsim = nsim)
result(gi)
giStrata <- genealogicalIndexTest(fad, trait = tcancer, traitName = "cancer", nsim = nsim, strata = fad$sex)
plotRes(giStrata)
giFam <- genealogicalIndexTest(fad, trait = tcancer, nsim = nsim, perFamilyTest = TRUE, traitName = "Cancer")
fr <- familialIncidenceRate(fad, trait = tcancer, timeAtRisk = mbsub$endage)
frTest <- familialIncidenceRateTest(fad, trait = tcancer, traitName = "cancer", timeAtRisk = mbsub$endage, nsim = nsim)
head(result(frTest))
kinSum <- kinshipSumTest(fad, trait = tcancer, traitName = "cancer", nsim = nsim, strata = fad$sex)
head(result(kinSum))
plotPed(kinSum, id = kinSumIds[1], cex = 0.3, only.phenotyped = TRUE)
plotRes(kinSum, id = kinSumIds[1])
kinGroup <- kinshipGroupTest(fad, trait = tcancer, traitName = "cancer", nsim = nsim, strata = fad$sex)
head(result(kinGroup))
plotPed(kinGroup, id = kinGroupRes[kinGroupRes$family == "432", "group_id"][1], prune = TRUE, label1 = fr)
binRes <- binomialTest(fad, trait = tcancer, traitName = "Cancer")
binResTab <- result(binRes)
